title: Himachal Pradesh fill 1: top places in Kullu, Parvati and Spiti
selection: Bijli Mahadev, Bajaura, Manikaran, Malana, Key, Tabo, Dhankar, Kibber, Langza, Chandratal and Pin Valley.

places.name: Basheshar Mahadev Temple, Bajaura
places.summary: A carved stone Shiva temple of the 9th–12th century on the Beas at Bajaura, just off the highway south of Kullu.
places.seoDescription: Basheshar (Vishveshvara) Mahadev at Bajaura: a 9th–12th-century stone Shiva temple on the Beas with fine bas-reliefs, close to the Kullu highway.

images.commons: File:0042523 Basheshar Mahadev Temple, Bajaura, Himachal Pradesh 058.jpg
images.alt: The carved stone tower of the Basheshar Mahadev temple at Bajaura
images.caption: Basheshar Mahadev, Bajaura

overview.text:
The Vishveshvara Mahadev temple at Bajaura — locally Basheshar — is a pyramidal stone temple to Shiva, dated to between the 9th and 12th century AD. It is one of the few old stone temples in a valley better known for wooden ones.

Come for the carving: large bas-reliefs and sculptural decoration cover the walls. The temple follows Shankaracharya's Panch Dev Puja tradition, in which five gods are worshipped in one place. It stands on the bank of the Beas, close to the highway, so it is an easy stop between Bhuntar and Kullu or on the way up from Mandi. Allow half an hour to walk round the outside and look closely at the carved panels.

items.title: Location
items.body: Bajaura, on the Beas beside the highway

places.name: Bijli Mahadev Temple
places.summary: A hilltop Shiva temple at about 2,460 m above Kullu, reached by a 3 km walk, with the Kullu and Parvati valleys on either side.
places.seoTitle: Bijli Mahadev Temple, Kullu: Walk, Views & Legend
places.seoDescription: Bijli Mahadev above Kullu: the 3 km walk from the road, the lightning legend, Kath-Kuni architecture and views over the Kullu and Parvati valleys.

images.alt: The wooden Bijli Mahadev temple with its tall deodar staff on a hilltop above Kullu
images.caption: Bijli Mahadev Temple

overview.text:
Bijli Mahadev sits on a ridge at about 2,460 m above Kullu, with the Kullu valley on one side and the Parvati valley on the other. The walk up gives some of the widest views in the valley.

The temple is built in the Kath-Kuni style of stone and timber, with a 60-foot deodar staff standing in front. Its name means 'lightning Shiva': lightning is said to strike the lingam and break it, and the priests piece it back together with homemade butter, pulse flour and cereal.

A 3 km walk from the last road reaches the top. Trekkers can come the long way from Naggar, via Jana village through dense deodar forest.

places.name: Chandratal Lake
places.summary: The crescent 'Lake of the Moon' at about 4,300 m below Kunzum Pass, open late May to early October, with summer camps.
places.seoDescription: Chandratal (Chandra Taal) at about 4,300 m: the road from Batal, the 2-hour walk from Kunzum Pass, the late May–early October season and tented camps.

images.commons: File:Chandra Taal (Lake), HP, India, D35 7333 nx01.jpg
images.alt: The blue crescent of Chandratal lake ringed by grassy slopes and scree mountains
images.caption: Chandratal

overview.text:
Chandra Taal, the 'Lake of the Moon', is a deep-blue crescent of water at about 4,300 m, north of Kunzum Pass. Strictly it lies in Lahaul's Chandra watershed, but most travellers see it on a Spiti trip. In spring and summer the slopes turn to meadow and shepherds bring their flocks.

It is open from late May to early October. A road branches off at Batal to a car park; the last 1 km is on foot. The nicer approach is the two-hour level walk from Kunzum Pass. Bedded tents near the lake run from June to October.

items.title: Walk
items.body: 2 hours from Kunzum Pass; last 1 km from the car park

places.name: Dhankar Monastery
places.summary: A monastery-fort hanging on a cliff at 3,370 m above the Spiti river, between Kaza and Tabo, with a walk to Dhankar Lake.
places.seoDescription: Dhankar Monastery in Spiti: the cliff-top fort of the Nono, Bhoti scriptures, the 7 km road from Schichling and the walk to Dhankar Lake.

images.alt: Dhankar monastery's buildings clinging to eroded cliffs above the Spiti valley
images.caption: Dhankar Gompa

overview.text:
Dhankar hangs dramatically on a cliff above the left bank of the Spiti river, on a 7 km side road from Schichling, between Kaza and Tabo. Dhankar means 'fort', and that is what it was: the monastery guarded the valley against invaders and served as the castle of the Nono, Spiti's ruler.

At 3,370 m it keeps Buddhist scriptures in the Bhoti script. The cliff-hugging complex shows off old Spitian building skill. Use it as a base: a trail climbs to Dhankar Lake, and the Pin valley turn-off is close by. Spiti's monastery-forts are a reminder that the valley was fought over by Kullu, Ladakh and an army from Jammu and Kashmir in 1841.

places.name: Key Monastery
places.summary: Spiti's largest monastery, a Gelugpa gompa stacked on a hill at 4,166 m, 12 km from Kaza.
places.seoTitle: Key Monastery (Kye Gompa), Spiti: Visit Guide
places.seoDescription: Key Monastery near Kaza: Spiti's largest gompa at 4,166 m, its thangkas, murals and Tangyur library, and how to combine it with Kibber.

images.alt: Key Monastery's whitewashed buildings rising up a conical hill above the Spiti valley
images.caption: Key Monastery

overview.text:
Key (Kye) Gompa is the largest monastery in Spiti, a Gelugpa establishment stacked on a hilltop at 4,166 m, 12 km from Kaza. It is still a training centre for young lamas.

Inside is a maze of faintly lit rooms and dark corridors. Old wooden columns and stone steps lead to carved doors and prayer chambers hung with rare thangkas and murals, and there are ancient musical instruments and a library of Tangyur manuscripts. The monastery has been plundered and rebuilt several times, starting with Mongol raids in the 17th century.

Pair it with Kibber, 6 km further on, and come in the morning, when the light on the hill and the valley below is at its best.

places.name: Kibber
places.summary: One of Spiti's highest villages at 4,205 m, 18 km from Kaza, gateway to the Kibber Sanctuary's snow leopard country.
places.seoTitle: Kibber Village, Spiti: Snow Leopard Country
places.seoDescription: Kibber at 4,205 m: one of Spiti's highest villages, the Kibber Sanctuary's blue sheep, ibex and snow leopards, the summer bus from Kaza and treks.

images.alt: Traditional whitewashed houses of Kibber village under bare brown mountains
images.caption: Kibber village

overview.text:
Kibber, at 4,205 m, is one of the highest inhabited villages in Spiti, 6 km past Key Monastery and 18 km from Kaza. Green fields and rows of matching whitewashed houses stand out against the arid hills.

Beyond the village lies the Kibber Sanctuary, about 1,400 sq km of habitat for blue sheep, ibex and snow leopards — the reason Kibber is known worldwide as a wildlife spot. It is also the starting point for several high-altitude treks.

A state bus runs from Kaza in summer; the village has a civil dispensary and a post office. Bring warm layers even in summer.

items.title: Bus
items.body: State bus from Kaza in summer

places.name: Langza
places.summary: A high Spiti village of mud houses watched over by a giant Buddha, known for ammonite fossils, 16 km from Kaza.
places.seoTitle: Langza, Spiti: Buddha Statue & Fossil Village
places.seoDescription: Langza near Kaza: the giant Buddha facing Chau Chau Kang Nilda, ammonite fossils, pottery and crafts, high lakes and the road on to Komic and Hikkim.

images.alt: A giant golden Buddha statue above the mud houses of Langza
images.caption: Langza and its Buddha

overview.text:
Langza is a village of mud houses 16 km from Kaza, guarded by a huge statue of the Buddha gazing out at the snow peak of Chau Chau Kang Nilda. It is best known for ammonite fossils, and for clay pottery, carpets and shawls made by villagers who live by handicrafts and farming.

Walk out from the village on trails to scenic high-altitude lakes. The tarred road continues past Langza to Komic, at 4,400 m one of the highest villages on a motorable road, and Hikkim, the valley's highest habitation, is reached from Komic. Together they make a good loop from Kaza.

items.title: Known for
items.body: Ammonite fossils, pottery, carpets and shawls

places.name: Malana
places.summary: A remote village at 2,652 m off the Parvati valley, with its own council, language and strict rules for visitors.
places.seoTitle: Malana Village: Rules, Route & What to Know
places.seoDescription: Malana above the Parvati valley: its own council and Kanashi language, the no-touch rule and fine, the road from Jari and the Chanderkhani Pass trek.

images.alt: Wooden houses of Malana village on a steep mountainside
images.caption: Malana village

overview.text:
Malana sits on a remote plateau at 2,652 m above the Malana river, in a side valley of the Parvati. For centuries it has run itself: a two-house village council settles affairs, and cases it cannot decide go to the local deity, Jamlu, whose oracle's word is final. Villagers speak Kanashi, a language unlike the Pahari of the rest of Kullu.

Visit with respect. Outsiders may not touch anything in the village — its people, houses or temples — and the fine is ₹2,500 to ₹3,500. The usual way in is by road from Jari; trekkers can come over the Chanderkhani Pass.

items.title: Access
items.body: By road from Jari, or over Chanderkhani Pass

items.title: Rule
items.body: Don't touch people, houses or temples; fine ₹2,500–3,500

places.name: Manikaran
places.summary: A Hindu and Sikh pilgrimage town on the Parvati, 4 km from Kasol, with a gurdwara and hot springs hot enough to cook rice.
places.seoTitle: Manikaran Sahib & Hot Springs, Parvati Valley
places.seoDescription: Manikaran near Kasol: the gurdwara, Raghunath temple and the boiling hot springs where rice is cooked, 40 km from Kullu.

images.commons: File:Manikaran Gurdwara, a Holy place for Shikhs at Manikaran 01.jpg
images.alt: Manikaran gurdwara on the bank of the Parvati with steam rising from the hot springs
images.caption: Manikaran Sahib on the Parvati

overview.text:
Manikaran sits on the Parvati at about 1,829 m, 4 km beyond Kasol and 40 km from Kullu, under high mountains. It is a pilgrimage town for both Hindus and Sikhs: the gurdwara honours Guru Nanak, who is said to have come here with five disciples, and the Raghunath temple draws Hindu pilgrims.

The hot springs are the marvel. The water is so hot that rice in a muslin bag, dropped into the pool, cooks, and the sulphur spring in the gurdwara's compound is believed to be therapeutic. Then walk the lanes of temples along the river. Legend links the name to an earring Parvati dropped here, which the serpent Shesha carried off into the earth.

places.name: Pin Valley National Park
places.summary: A 675 sq km park of high valleys south of Dhankar: snow leopard and ibex country, Kungri monastery and the village of Mud.
places.seoTitle: Pin Valley National Park, Spiti: Mud & Kungri
places.seoDescription: Pin Valley National Park in Spiti: snow leopard, ibex and bharal, the road from Atargoo to Mud, Kungri monastery's thangkas and the Pin Parbati Pass trek.

images.commons: File:Pin Valley Spiti Himachal Jun18 D72 7092.jpg
images.alt: The wide Pin valley with its braided river and bare mountains in Spiti
images.caption: Pin Valley

overview.text:
The Pin river carves a side valley south of Dhankar, and the whole of it is a national park: 675 sq km, set up in 1987, rising from about 3,500 m to over 6,000 m. More than twenty rare species live here, including the snow leopard, ibex and bharal.

A narrow road leaves the main valley at Atargoo, 10 km from Schichling, and runs past Kungri — a 14th-century Nyingma monastery with over 380 thangkas and a Devil and Sword dance every July — to the village of Mud. From here tough treks cross the Pin Parbati Pass into Kullu.

items.title: Festival
items.body: Kungri's Devil and Sword dance, July

places.name: Tabo Monastery
places.summary: Founded in 996 AD, the oldest continuously working Buddhist monastery in the Himalayas, with famous murals, 48 km from Kaza.
places.seoDescription: Tabo Monastery in Spiti: founded 996 AD, nine temples and 23 chortens, wall paintings and stucco statues, the meditation caves and the distance from Kaza.

images.alt: Mud-walled temples of Tabo Monastery in the desert village of Tabo
images.caption: Tabo Monastery

overview.text:
Tabo was founded in 996 AD and is the largest monastic complex in Spiti: nine temples, 23 chortens, a monks' chamber and a nuns' chamber, set in a village of apple orchards in the cold desert. It is noted as the oldest continuously operating Buddhist enclave in India and the Himalayas, and is protected by the Archaeological Survey of India.

Inside the old mud temples are galleries of wall paintings and stucco statues; daily prayers now happen in a newer assembly hall. On the hillside opposite, look for the caves where monks once meditated in solitude for months. Tabo is 48 km from Kaza, and the first big stop when you come in from Kinnaur.
